text: Add request tab as one categorical scoring feature alongside user_id and video_id.
rationale: Tab is an impression-time request-context value and is the narrowest confirmation of the only feature family with a positive, full-coverage train-only temporal screen.
exact_ablation: In data.py, append only tab to FIELDS, fit its vocabulary on training rows only, and leave the additive model, optimizer, loss, and all other settings unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.003, because tab varies across a user's scored impressions and may improve context-conditional ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.000 to +0.002, with a smaller expected effect because the screen did not separately establish top-five improvement.

text: Add hour-of-week request timing as one categorical scoring feature alongside user_id and video_id.
rationale: The completed request-context screen includes hour and weekday, has full coverage, and was positive on each of four internal temporal-holdout days; a single timing encoding isolates that mechanism.
exact_ablation: Append only a training-vocabulary categorical hour_of_week derived from request-time hour and weekday to FIELDS; retain the additive scorer, BCE training, and seed hyperparameters unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.003 from time-specific user/item preference ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: 0.000 to +0.002 if temporal preference promotes positives into the top five; it may be flatter than GAUC.

text: Add weekday as one categorical scoring feature alongside user_id and video_id.
rationale: Weekday is a low-cardinality request-time signal inside the sole prioritized feature group, making it a cheap, interpretable test of recurring consumption context.
exact_ablation: Append only weekday to FIELDS with a seven-value training-fitted vocabulary; make no model, loss, sampling, or optimization change.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.000 to +0.002, expected to be weaker than tab or hour-of-week because weekday is coarse.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: 0.000 to +0.001, with risk of no detectable change at rank five.

text: Add the predeclared request-context family of tab, hour, and weekday to the seed scorer.
rationale: This is the strongest directly measured direction: request_context produced a +0.002213 primary lift in the train-only temporal screen with 1.0 coverage and positive lift on all four screen days.
exact_ablation: Append exactly tab, hour, and weekday as categorical fields to the seed feature matrix, with all vocabularies fitted on training only; retain the additive scorer and BCE objective unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.002 to +0.004, expected to be the dominant component of the screened primary lift.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.003, but explicitly gate on this metric because the screen evidence is primary-level rather than top-five-specific.

text: Replace the additive user-plus-video scorer with a two-field factorization-machine interaction scorer.
rationale: The seed's additive ID terms cannot represent user-video compatibility, whereas official metrics require score variation among a user's candidate items. This changes the interaction mechanism rather than merely increasing width.
exact_ablation: Replace Model.logits with bias plus linear user/video terms plus one learned dot product between user_id and video_id embeddings; keep the same input fields, pointwise BCE target, optimizer type, and early-stop proxy.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.003 to +0.008 because personalized user-video interactions directly alter within-user item order.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.002 to +0.006 if interaction scores elevate relevant videos near the top; sparse IDs may limit this.

text: Replace unweighted row-level BCE with per-user normalized BCE.
rationale: The official GAUC is within-user and positive-count weighted, while the seed's row-mean BCE can be dominated by highly active users. This objective-only change tests whether more balanced user influence improves ranking.
exact_ablation: Keep the seed model and features unchanged, but weight each training row's BCE by the inverse number of that user's training rows and normalize by total weight.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.004 if prolific users currently dominate the pointwise objective.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.002 because equal-user weighting is not explicitly top-five optimized and can trade off head-user ranking.

text: Replace pointwise BCE with within-user positive-negative RankNet loss using only training impressions.
rationale: GAUC measures positive-versus-negative ordering within user, so a user-local pairwise objective is more aligned than independent row calibration. No direct current loss comparison exists; screen evidence establishes only the measured ID-based starting representation.
exact_ablation: Keep seed features and scorer unchanged, replace BCE with a deterministic RankNet logistic loss over sampled positive-negative pairs from the same training user, cap at four negatives per positive, and never form cross-user pairs.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.002 to +0.006 from direct positive-negative ordering pressure.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: 0.000 to +0.003; it can remain flat or decline because uniform pair sampling does not prioritize top-five inversions.

text: Add an nDCG@5-swap-weighted pairwise term to the seed BCE objective.
rationale: The supplied diagnostic assessment says GAUC is stronger than top-five ordering, particularly for cold users. A top-five-weighted pairwise term is a targeted objective mechanism, though the available measured feature screen does not directly validate it.
exact_ablation: Keep the seed representation and BCE loss, and add one detached within-user positive-negative RankNet term weighted by each pair's absolute nDCG@5 swap delta, using lambda=0.25 and train rows only.

expected_effect.GAUC: 0.000 to +0.003; top-rank emphasis may leave broad pair ordering mostly unchanged.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.002 to +0.006 if positives near rank five are promoted; this is the primary intended effect.

text: Add a causally constructed recent-prior-video-ID mean-pooling history feature.
rationale: A history representation can personalize candidate scores beyond static user ID while using only previous impressions. It deliberately excludes all engagement outcomes, and it does not reuse the screened-negative historical author or item response rates.
exact_ablation: For every row, construct from only strictly earlier impressions of the same user a padded sequence of the latest 20 video IDs, mean-pool their embeddings, and add the pooled-vector dot product with the candidate video embedding to the seed logit; use no current or prior outcome labels in the history.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.005 if prior exposure sequence encodes repeatable preference.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.004 if recent exposures identify immediate intent; sparse-history users may see no benefit.

text: Replace uniform row minibatches with a deterministic positive-stratified minibatch sampler for BCE.
rationale: The seed trains on a binary long-view target and may produce low-positive batches. This sampling-only ablation tests optimization stability without altering features, labels, or the official evaluation population.
exact_ablation: Keep model, BCE definition, and all examples unchanged, but construct each training minibatch with a fixed 1:3 positive-to-negative row ratio through deterministic oversampling of training positives, with importance weights restoring the original row-level BCE expectation.

expected_effect.GAUC: 0.000 to +0.003 if rare-positive gradients are presently underrepresented.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: 0.000 to +0.002; increased score separation can help top five, but importance-weight variance may erase the gain.

text: Apply exponential recency weighting to training BCE using only the training-row date.
rationale: The official split is temporal, so emphasizing recent training observations is a concrete distribution-shift adaptation. The request-context screen's day-to-day lift variability supports treating temporal robustness as uncertain rather than assuming stationarity.
exact_ablation: Keep seed features and model unchanged, but multiply each training BCE contribution by exp(-age_days/7), where age is measured relative to the final training date, and normalize the weights to mean one.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.003 depending on whether late-training preferences better match validation.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.002; recency can improve freshness alignment but reduce effective sample size.

text: Use a warm-started within-user hard-pair curriculum instead of uniform pair selection.
rationale: This targets residual local ordering errors and is intended to improve top-five quality more than broad GAUC. It is explicitly exploratory because there is no scored pairwise parent and the only measured positive signal is request context.
exact_ablation: Keep seed features and scorer unchanged; train RankNet pairs within each training user with two uniform-pair warm-start epochs, followed by 50% uniform and 50% lowest-margin pairs refreshed from the prior epoch's train-only checkpoint.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.003 because concentrating on difficult pairs can reduce broad ordering coverage.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.005 if hard pairs correspond to local high-rank inversions; noisy implicit labels are a substantial failure mode.
